And of the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Jonas.
Of the temple singers: Eliashib and Bacchurus.{l}
Of the gatekeepers: Shallum and Tolbanes.
Of Israel, of the sons of Parosh: Hiermas, Jeddias, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Hashabiah, and Benaiah.{m}
Of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jezrielus, Obadiah, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
And of the sons of Zamoth: Eliadas, Eliashib, Othoniah, Jerimoth, Sabathus, and Zeralias.
And of the sons of Bebai: Johanan, Hananiah, Zabdus, and Emathis.
And of the sons of Mani: Olamus, Mamuchus, Jedaeus, Jashub, Asaelus, and Jeremoth.
And of the sons of Addi: Naathus, Moossias, Laccunus, Naidus, Bescaspasmys, Sesthel, Balnuus, and Manasseas.{n}
And of the sons of Annan: Elionas, Asaeas, Malchijah, Sabbaeas, and Simon Chosamaeus.
And of the sons of Hashum: Maltannaeus, Mattathias, Sabannaeus, Eliphalat, Manasseh, Semei.

And of the sons of Bani: Jeremai, Momdis, Maerus, Joel, Mamdai, Bedeiah, Vaniah, Carabasion, Enasibus, Mamnitanaemus, Eliasis, Binnui, Elialis, Shimei, Shelemiah, and Nethaniah. And of the sons of Ezora: Shashai, Azarel, Azael, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Joseph.{o}
Of the sons of Nooma: Mazitias, Zabadaeas, Iddo, Joel, and Benaiah.
Every one of these had taken foreign wives, and they sent them away with the children.{p}

And the priests and the Levites and those of Israel settled in Jerusalem and in the country. On the new moon of the seventh month (September–October),{q} when the sons of Israel were in their settlements,
the whole multitude came together as one man into the broad place before the temple gate toward the east;{r}
and they bade Ezra, priest and reader, fetch the law of Moses that the God of Israel had handed down.
So Ezra the chief priest{s} brought the law to all the multitude, both men and women, and to all the priests, that they might hear the law, on the new moon of the seventh month.
And from early morning until noon he read in the broad place in front of the temple gate, before men and women alike; and they gave all their attention to the law.
And Ezra the priest and reader of the law stood upon the wooden platform which had been made for the purpose;
and there stood beside him on his right Mattathias, Sammus, Hananiah, Azariah, Uriah, Hezekiah, and Baalsamus;
and on his left Phaldaeus, Mishael, Malchijah, Lothasubus, Nabariah, and Zechariah.
Then Ezra took up the book in the sight of the multitude, for he sat in the place of honor in the sight of all;
and when he opened the law, they all stood upright. And Azariah{t} blessed the Lord, the Most High God, the God of hosts, the Almighty;{u}
and all the multitude answered, “Amen, amen!” And lifting up their hands they fell to the ground and worshiped the Lord.

Jeshua, Anniuth, Sarabias, Jadinus, Jarsubus, Abtaeus, Autaeas, Maiannas, Calitas, Azarias, Jozabdus, Annias, Phalias, the Levites, taught the law of the Lord, and read the law of the Lord to the multitude, at the same time giving the sense of what was read.{v}
And Attharates{w} spoke to Ezra, high priest and reader, and to the Levites who instructed the people, and to everyone:
“This day is holy to the Lord”; for they were all weeping as they heard the law.{x}
“Go then, and eat the fat and drink the sweet, and send portions to those who have none;
for the day is holy to the Lord; and do not be sorrowful, for the Lord will glorify you.”
The Levites likewise gave charge to the whole people: “This day is holy; be not grieved.”
Then they all went their way to eat and drink and make merry, and to give portions to those who had none, and to rejoice greatly;
for the words they had been taught had filled them with fervor. And they came together.{y}

notes.text: Greek “the chamber of Jonas the son of Naseibos” (Swete); Ezra 10:6 has Jehohanan the son of Eliashib, whose names are followed here. Jehohanan means “Yahweh is gracious”; Eliashib means “God restores.”
Greek “devoted” or “consecrated” (aniĕrōthēsontai), that is, forfeited to the sanctuary; compare Ezra 10:8, “all his property should be forfeited.”
Greek “this was the ninth month, on the twentieth of the month,” that is, Kislev, on the spring-start calendar (Ezra 10:9).
Greek “trembling because of the present winter”; Ezra 10:9 adds “because of this matter and because of the heavy rain.” Kislev falls in the rainy season.
Greek “and we have not found (it),” an obscure phrase; the sense may be that they have not been able to complete the task, or that there is no shelter.

Greek “Jonathas son of Azaelus and Ezekias son of Thokanos”; the names follow Ezra 10:15. Jonathan means “Yahweh has given”; Tikvah means “hope.” In Ezra 10:15 these men oppose the plan; here they carry it out.
Greek “on the new moon of the tenth month,” that is, Tevet, on the spring-start calendar (Ezra 10:16).
Greek “until the new moon of the first month,” that is, Nisan, on the spring-start calendar (Ezra 10:17). The examination thus took about three months.

Greek Maeēlas, Eleazaros, Ioribos, Iōdanos; the forms of Ezra 10:18 (Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, Gedaliah) are partly followed. 9:18–36 parallels the list of Ezra 10:18–44; many names differ, and the Greek forms are generally kept in this list.
That is, they pledged themselves (Ezra 10:19).
Swete’s forms are Phaisur, Elionais, Asseias, Ismaelos, Nathanaelos, Okaildos, Salthas; compare Ezra 10:22 (Pashhur, Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, Elasah).
Swete has Eliasebos and Bakchouros; Ezra 10:24 names only Eliashib among the singers.
Swete has Phoros (Parosh), Ierma, Iezeias, Melcheias, Milelos, Eleazaros, Asebeias, Bannaias; compare Ezra 10:25.
Swete has Addein; Ezra 10:30 has Pahath-moab. The Greek list in this verse differs considerably from Ezra.

In Swete the list runs to the end of verse 35, and the sons of Ezora are part of verse 34. Swete’s forms here include Ierēmias, Momdeios, Maēros, Iouna, Mamdai, Pedias, Anōs, Karabaseion, Enaseibos, Mamtanaimos, Eliaseis, Bannous, Edialeis, Someeis, Selemias, Nathanias; and for the sons of Ezora, Seseis, Ezreil, Azaēlos, Samatos, Zambrei, Phosēpos. Some forms are adapted toward Ezra 10:34–42.
Greek “and they sent them away with children.” Ezra 10:44 ends with an obscure Hebrew clause, often rendered “and some of the wives had borne children.”

Greek “on the new moon of the seventh month,” that is, Tishri, on the spring-start calendar. 9:37–55 parallels Nehemiah 7:73–8:12. In 1 Esdras, Nehemiah does not appear in this scene; see the note on verse 49.
Nehemiah 8:1 has “the square before the Water Gate.”
Greek archiereus, “high priest”; in Nehemiah 8:2 Ezra is called “the priest.”
Azariah is not in Nehemiah 8:6, where Ezra himself blesses the Lord; Azariah has been named among those standing beside him (verse 43).

Greek Pantokratōr, “ruler of all,” the Septuagint word for the Hebrew Sabaoth (“of hosts”) and Shaddai; “Almighty” renders it in this translation. Swete reads simply “the Most High God, the Almighty”; “the Lord … the God of hosts” follows Nehemiah 8:6 and other Greek copies, as reported.

Greek emphysiountes, literally “breathing into” the reading, that is, making it come alive and giving its meaning (compare Nehemiah 8:8, “they gave the sense, so that the people understood the reading”).
Greek Attharatēs, a corrupt form of the Persian title tirshatha, “governor,” given to Nehemiah in Nehemiah 8:9 (compare 1 Esdras 5:40, Attharias). 1 Esdras treats it as a personal name.
Nehemiah 8:9 has “Do not mourn or weep,” and explains, “for all the people wept when they heard the words of the law.”

The book ends abruptly in the middle of the Nehemiah narrative (Nehemiah 8:12–13). The last words, “And they assembled together,” correspond to the start of Nehemiah 8:13 and suggest that the end of the book has been lost; the work may originally have continued with the Feast of Booths. Josephus, who used 1 Esdras for his account of this period (Antiquities 11), reportedly continues the story to Ezra’s death.
